new_statements.quote: Wat betreft de tonetiek van het alhier besproken Luba-Katanga, deze wijkt nauwelijks af van de algemene regels, welke BURSSENS voor het Luba-Kasayi heeft vastgesteld. De middentoon blijkt meestentijds slechts als variant te fungeren van één der monotonemen : hoog ≶ laag, zowel grammatisch als semantisch, zodat de rol van het dynamische intensiteitsaccent, evenals in het Luba-Kasayi, op een ondergeschikt plan wordt teruggedrongen. new_statements.translation: As regards the tonetics of the Luba-Katanga treated here, it hardly deviates from the general rules that Burssens established for Luba-Kasayi. The mid tone turns out mostly to function merely as a variant of one of the monotonemes, high vs. low, both grammatically and semantically, so that the role of the dynamic intensity accent [stress], just as in Luba-Kasayi, is pushed back to a subordinate level. Finally the author devotes a well-documented survey to the influence that tonemes and prosodemes can exert on the syntactic units.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Luba-Katanga is a tone language (H vs L, mid tone a conditioned variant); dynamic (intensity) stress plays only a subordinate role, as in Luba-Kasai. No position for word stress is stated.
new_statements.domain_note: A reviewer's summary characterisation based on the dictionary's introduction (Van Avermaet & Mbuya 1954, pp. vii-xvi), Van Avermaet 1945 and Burssens's work; not a placement rule and not the describer's own fieldwork. The dictionary's informant B. Mbuya came from Kabondo-Dianda; Blok notes Beckett 1951's dialect is closest.
new_statements.identity_note: Blok's 1955 remark concerns Luba-Katanga (L33) as recorded in Van Avermaet & Mbuya 1954 (informant from Kabondo-Dianda; Blok says Beckett 1951's dialect material is the closest match). Van Avermaet 1945 describes kiLuba Samba (Basamba area; Glottolog misfiles this article under luba1249 but lists the anonymous 'Beknopte grammatica van het kiluba-samba' under luba1250). Mutonkole 1994 = Malemba-Nkulu II dialect; Ilunga Bwana 2019 = Kabongo (Haut-Lomami) variety. Colle 1913's 'accent tonique.. sur la pénultième ou l'antépénultième' concerns Baluba-Hemba / kiluba-hemba (eastern Luba of the White Fathers' missions), which Glottolog files under Hemba (hemb1242), and Van Avermaet 1945 judged it a confusion of tone with accent; it should not be entered for luba1250. Yukawa 1992 'Luba' = Ciluba (luba1249).
